instruction: Locate and bookmark the personal homepages of the first three authors listed in the paper, organizing them in a folder called 'Lead Authors'.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL SEMANTIC ERROR: Folder name hardcoded mismatch - instruction requires folder named 'Lead Authors' but metric function is_expected_bookmarks (chrome.py:221) has 'Liked Authors' hardcoded, completely ignoring the rule['names'] parameter
The metric function extracts rule['names'] containing 'Lead Authors' but line 221 performs a hardcoded check: bookmark['name'] == 'Liked Authors', making the names parameter useless
Consequence: Even if user correctly creates 'Lead Authors' folder with all correct author website bookmarks, evaluator will always return 0.0 because it searches for wrong folder name
This is a fundamental logic error in the metric function that makes verification impossible for this instruction - the evaluator cannot verify what the instruction actually requires
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Fix chrome.py:221 in is_expected_bookmarks function - replace hardcoded string 'Liked Authors' with dynamic lookup from rule['names'] parameter
Change line 221 from: bookmark['name'] == 'Liked Authors' to: bookmark['name'] in rule['names']
This will make the evaluator properly check for the folder name specified in the rules, which is 'Lead Authors' for this task
Alternative fix: Change line 221 to: bookmark['name'] == rule.get('names', ['Liked Authors'])[0] with proper fallback
